In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (i) the CP violation parameter ϵ ′, (ii) the right-handed quark mass matrix, (iii) the left–right symmetry breaking, and (iv) the left– right symmetry scale.
the study of the CP violation in the K → π π decays within the framework of the left–right symmetry.
the study of CP violation in the minimal left-right symmetric model (LRS) in which both left- and right-handed gauge interactions are present.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the minimal left-right symmetric model, the direct CP violation parameter ϵ ′ is suppressed relative to the standard model by a factor ∼ M 2 W / M 2 W R, where M W R > > M W.
the left-right symmetric scale M W L R is at least 5 TeV.
the minimal left– right model with the recently obtained right-handed quark CKM mixing is in agreement with the data on ϵ and ϵ ′, and that the scale of the right-handed gauge bosons is above 5 TeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimal left– right symmetric model is a natural candidate for new physics beyond the standard model.
a new physics scale of 5 TeV can be tested in K-decays.
the left–right scale M W R is constrained to be larger than 5 TeV, and that the right-handed mixing angle is constrained to be smaller than 0.02.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the minimal left– right symmetry scale M W R can be constrained by the direct CP-violating parameter ϵ ′, and that the constraint is robust and independent of the details of the model.
the direct CP-violating parameter ϵ ′ is sensitive to the right-handed sector of the theory, and can be used to constrain new physics scales.

the minimal left– right model can be tested by the direct CP-violating parameter ϵ ′, and if the scale of new physics is not far above the TeV scale, then the model can be tested with the existing data.
